name: YACSS
subcategory: programmatic site generation and cloud stacking
tagline: Type a keyword, get a full static HTML site with AI content, schema and on-page SEO, then push copies onto free cloud hosts for backlinks.

pricing.basis: monthly, per account, with site and upload quotas
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Higher agency tier reportedly exists with larger quotas.

verdictSummary: The generator half of this is genuinely a one-shot: keyword in, LLM out, templated static HTML with JSON-LD, internal links, sitemap and city page permutations is a solved evening of work. The part you cannot build in a session is the distribution machinery: authenticated uploads into dozens of free cloud properties across pooled Google, Amazon and Microsoft accounts, plus the constant repair work when those properties change their upload paths or start rejecting bulk junk. Rank tracking and expired domain data are separate data problems you would be paying someone else for anyway. So you can absolutely own the content factory locally and drop the subscription if you are happy deploying to your own hosts. If the specific thing you want is cloud stacking at volume, the tool is mostly a maintenance contract on other people's platforms, and you are renting that maintenance.
coreLoopDIY: A local CLI that takes a keyword, plans a topic cluster, generates page copy and JSON-LD with an LLM, and writes a complete interlinked static site plus sitemap and robots into a dist folder ready to deploy anywhere.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Optional image API key or placeholder images
Somewhere to host the output: your own S3 bucket, Pages host or VPS
whatYouLose: Automated uploads to many third party cloud hosts, which is the actual product
Pooled Gmail and Drive connections so uploads run across many accounts
GBP rank tracking and expired domain lookups
Ongoing fixes when a cloud platform changes its uploader or blocks bulk content
A browser UI for editing sites you already pushed live
moatNotes: The moat is not the AI writing, it is knowing which free cloud properties still accept uploads this month and having the plumbing to hit them at volume without hand-managing logins.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because agencies are buying throughput and upkeep, not text generation. Generating four hundred sites is trivial; getting them onto a hundred different Google, Amazon and Microsoft surfaces without personally clicking through a hundred consent screens is not, and that pipeline breaks constantly as platforms tighten. Add rank tracking and expired domain data that nobody wants to source themselves, and $199 a month is cheaper than one person babysitting uploaders. Worth noting the whole method leans on other companies' free tiers and on search guidelines that were not written with this in mind, so you are also paying for someone else to absorb that risk.
notes: You can build the printing press in an evening; the distribution network is the business.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called sitegen that generates complete static SEO sites from a keyword.

Stack, no substitutions: Node 20, TypeScript, tsx for running, Eta for HTML templates, Zod for validating LLM output, the OpenAI SDK for generation. No web UI, no database, no accounts, no telemetry. Everything runs from the terminal and writes files to disk.

Commands:
1. `sitegen plan "keyword"` : calls the model once to produce a site plan as JSON: site title, meta description, a pillar page, 8 to 20 cluster pages each with slug, title, meta description, H2 outline and internal link targets. Validate with Zod, save to `sites/<slug>/plan.json`. Never overwrite an existing plan without --force.
2. `sitegen build <slug>` : for each page in the plan, generate body HTML from the outline (semantic markup only: h1, h2, p, ul, table), render through an Eta layout, and write to `sites/<slug>/dist/<page-slug>/index.html`. Concurrency limit 4, retry twice on API failure, cache each page's generated body in `sites/<slug>/cache/` keyed by a hash of its outline so rebuilds are free.
3. `sitegen local <slug> --city-list cities.txt` : clone a designated template page per city, substituting city name, a static embedded Google Maps directions iframe URL built from the city, and a short list of points of interest from the model.
4. `sitegen serve <slug>` : plain static file server on port 4321 for previewing.

Every page must include: one h1, a title and meta description, canonical link, Open Graph tags, breadcrumb JSON-LD, and Article or LocalBusiness JSON-LD chosen by page type. Build also writes sitemap.xml, robots.txt and a homepage that links every page, plus contextual internal links between cluster pages and the pillar.

Images: if UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY is set in .env, fetch one hero image per page and write descriptive alt text from the page title; otherwise generate a local SVG placeholder. Never hotlink.

Secrets in .env only (OPENAI_API_KEY, optional UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY), with .env.example committed and .env gitignored.

Explicitly out of scope: uploading anywhere, OAuth to any cloud provider, multi account management, rank tracking, expired domain lookups. Deployment is the user's problem; just print the dist path when the build finishes.

Include a README with setup, a worked example run, and a one paragraph note that mass generated sites pointed at your own properties are a search guideline risk the user owns.
